text: A lowercase LEI is valid and distinct from its uppercase twin.

comments.text: The design reads 'alphanumeric' literally, so "abcdefghij0123456789" and "ABCDEFGHIJ0123456789" count as two different LEIs. Real LEIs are uppercase ISO 17442 codes. Under this rule, P1 ('belongs to one legal entity only') lets one real-world LEI sit on two legal entities, differing only in case. The design states the choice, but Open Questions says 'None' and the spec author never confirmed it. Add it to the points flagged for the author. Ask whether lowercase is rejected (R1) or uniqueness is compared case-insensitively (P1). Task 1 and Task 3 then follow whichever answer comes back.

The design takes 'alphanumeric' literally (ASCII letters and digits, case-sensitive) because the spec fixes no case rule. Whether lowercase should be rejected under R1, or compared case-insensitively under P1, is a requirement the spec lane owns. The plan would change only in `LegalEntityRules` and its tests. Leaving this thread open for the spec author.
